title: Night Flight 1
content:
Inside the largest spiritual treasure pavilion in Lanling City.

Amidst rows upon rows of tiered, impeccably arranged curios shelves sat displays of countless high-grade spiritual jades and pristine, deadly weapons. Scores of cultivators milled about, scrutinizing items, comparing prices, and whenever they caught a free second, trading the latest gossip.

"Chief Cultivator?" one man mused aloud. "Seems like the prominent sects have been screaming at each other over this for weeks. Has anything actually been settled?"

"What's there to argue about? We can't stay a scattered heap of sand without a head forever. Appointing a single Chief Cultivator to lead the sects sounds like a solid idea to me."

"I don't know, feels a bit risky. What if we end up with another Qishan Wen Sect on our hands...?"

"How is that even remotely the same? The Chief Cultivator will be elected by a joint vote of all the sects. Totally different."

"Oh, please. 'Elected'? We all know how this works. At the end of the day, it's just the same handful of giants fighting for the throne. You think anyone else gets a say?"

"Chifeng-zun has been pushing back hard, hasn't he? Shot down Jin Guangshan's subtle and not-so-subtle hints countless times. Mark my words, this is going to drag on."

"Besides, only one person can sit on that throne. Even if the proposal passes, who actually gets the seat? We'll be listening to them bicker for another three years."

"Well, that's for the higher-ups to lose sleep over. Has nothing to do with little shrimps like us anyway."

Another cultivator pivoted the conversation: "Did anyone here attend the celebration for the reconstructed Library Pavilion at the Cloud Recesses last month? I went. Standing in front of it, I swear it was an exact replica of the original. No small feat, truly."

"Yeah, not easy at all. An ancestral estate of that scale, a centuries-old celestial paradise—you can't just throw that back up overnight."

"Speaking of which, there’ve been an awful lot of happy occasions lately."

"You mean the one-year catch ceremony for Jin Zixuan's boy? Out of that whole pile of colorful trinkets, the little prince went straight for his father's sword, Suihua! His parents were thrilled to tears, already swearing he's destined to be an unmatched grandmaster of the blade."

Not far off, a man dressed in crisp white robes was turning a jade-tasseled pendant over in his hands, examining it closely. Hearing the chatter, a soft, amused smile tugged at his lips.

A female cultivator’s voice drifted over from nearby: "Young Madame Jin really hit the jackpot in life... She must have given up her own ascension in her past life to cash in on this much good karma."

Her companion chimed in with a slight sneer, "Turns out, you can have all the virtues in the world, but nothing beats being born lucky. I mean, let's be real, she's utterly plain..."

The man in white frowned faintly. Fortunately, the sour gossip was drowned out by a boisterous voice across the aisle: "The Lanling Jin Sect never disappoints, does it? Throwing an extravagant bash like that for a mere one-year-old."

"Look at who the kid's parents are! How could they cut corners? Forget Young Madame Jin's husband refusing to cheap out—if the event were even a fraction less opulent, do you think her mother-in-law or her hot-tempered brother would let it slide? Just wait for the full-month banquet in two days; it's going to be twice as lavish."

"By the way, have you heard? Rumor has it... a certain someone was invited."

"Who?"

"Wei Wuxian!"

The entire treasure pavilion fell dead silent.

Someone gasped in sheer disbelief, "Wait... I thought that was just wild street gossip! Did they actually invite him?!"

"They did! It was confirmed just a few days ago—Wei Wuxian is attending."

"What the hell is the Lanling Jin Sect thinking?! Did they completely wipe the slaughter at Qiongqi Path from their memories?"

"Inviting a monster like that to Jin Ling's full-month banquet? Who would even dare show their face? I sure as hell wouldn't go."

The moment the words left his mouth, plenty of onlookers silently mocked him in their heads: As if you'd ever be worthy of an invitation in the first place. Who asked you to worry about going?

The man in white arched an amused brow. Having finalized his purchase, he stepped out of the pavilion into the bright daylight.

Turning down a quiet side alley a few paces away, a slender figure in black materialized from the shadows. "Gongzi, did you get what you needed?"

Wei Wuxian tossed the polished sandalwood box his way. Wen Ning caught it, popping the lid to reveal a delicate white-jade tassel pendant. The jade was translucent and milky, catching the sunlight with a soft, liquid sheen, as if humming with quiet life.

Wen Ning’s eyes lit up. "It's gorgeous!"

Wei Wuxian scoffed, "Pretty little trinkets like this don't come cheap. After buying a fresh set of clothes, your sister's purse barely covered the tag. We are officially down to our last copper coin—prepare to get your ears boxed when we get back."

Wen Ning hurriedly shook his head. "No, no. You're bringing a gift for Lady Jiang's child; Jiejie won't scold you for that."

"You said it, not me," Wei Wuxian warned, pointing a finger. "When she starts yelling, you'd better throw yourself in front of me."

Wen Ning nodded earnestly. "Young Master Jin Ling will definitely love it."

"This isn't the actual gift," Wei Wuxian dismissed. "It's just an accessory. Everything in that pavilion is all flash and no substance—what real use does it have?"

Wen Ning blinked, bewildered. "Then what did you prepare for the gift?"

Wei Wuxian tapped his nose with a sly smirk. "Heaven's secrets must not be leaked."

"Oh."

Wen Ning obediently shut his mouth. Wei Wuxian stood there waiting for a few seconds before his own patience snapped. "Wen Ning, aren't you supposed to follow up with relentless curiosity and beg for details? How can you just say 'oh' and drop it?! Don't you want to know what it is?!"

Wen Ning stared at him blankly, finally catching on. "...I do! Gongzi! What did you make?!"

Only then did Wei Wuxian smoothly pull a small wooden box from his sleeve, dangling it before Wen Ning’s eyes with a smug grin. Wen Ning took it, unclasped the latch, and gasped: "What an incredible silver clarity bell!"

By "incredible," he didn't merely mean its breathtaking craftsmanship. While the unblemished silver and the nine-petal lotus etched along its curved surface were undeniably the work of a master artisan, what truly stunned him was the dense, crackling wave of protective spiritual power sealed within the tiny bell.

Wen Ning looked up. "Gongzi, you locked yourself inside the Demon-Subduing Cave for over two weeks, losing track of day and night... just to forge this?"

"Naturally," Wei Wuxian said, puffed up with pride. "The moment my little nephew wears this bell, low-level spirits, wraiths, and monsters won't be able to step within three paces of him. You can't touch it, by the way—even a fierce corpse of your caliber would get a nasty shock."

Wen Ning nodded. "I can feel the bite on it."

Wei Wuxian retrieved the jade tassel, looping its silk cord through the base of the silver bell. The twin treasures complemented each other flawlessly, leaving him thoroughly pleased with his handiwork.

Wen Ning fidgeted, murmuring with slight hesitation, "Still... since you're attending Young Master Jin Ling's banquet, Gongzi, when you see Lady Jiang's husband... please try to hold your temper. Don't pick a fight with him..."

Wei Wuxian waved a dismissive hand. "Relax, I know how to behave. Seeing as Jin Zixuan actually had the decency to invite me, I won't utter a single bad word about him for an entire year."

Wen Ning scratched his head, offering a shy, apologetic smile. "When Young Master Jin dispatched a runner to deliver the invitation to the foot of the Burial Mounds, I genuinely thought it was an ambush. Turns out I misjudged him completely. Who knew he was actually a good man at heart..."

By high noon, the two reached Qiongqi Path.

Following its bloody renovation, the gorge had long since been renamed, though Wei Wuxian hadn't bothered to learn the new title. Nobody else seemed to remember it either, so people still defaulted to calling it Qiongqi Path. At first, nothing seemed amiss. But as they pressed deeper into the heart of the canyon, an uneasy prickle crept up Wei Wuxian’s spine.

There shouldn't be this few travelers on the road.

Wei Wuxian muttered, "Notice anything?"

Wen Ning’s pupils rolled upward into a stark, milky white. A beat later, the dark irises settled back into place. "Nothing. It's too quiet."

"Way too quiet," Wei Wuxian agreed.

He couldn't even catch the faint, ambient static of wandering spirits that usually buzzed in his ears.

Every instinct screaming, Wei Wuxian barked in a low hiss: "Move!"

He pivoted on his heel, but before he could take a stride, Wen Ning’s hand shot out like iron, snatching something right out of the air.

A fletched iron arrow—aimed dead center at Wei Wuxian's heart!

Wei Wuxian’s head snapped up. Emerging from the craggy ridges along the cliffs, crawling out from every crevice and rocky outcrop, were scores of armed men. Nearly three hundred cultivators. Most wore the golden Sparks Amidst Snow robes of Lanling Jin, though a few other sect colors dotted the ranks. Longbows drawn, spiritual swords at their hips, they were armed to the teeth, eyes blazing with cold malice. Using the high ground as cover, hundreds of nocked arrows and unsheathed blades were leveled directly at the two below.

Standing at the vantage point, longbow in hand, was the man who had loosed the opening shot. Tall, broad-shouldered, and swarthy, his handsome features were twisted in a familiar sneer.

Wei Wuxian tilted his chin up. "Who are you supposed to be?"

The archer had clearly prepared a grand, dramatic speech, but having his face completely blanked derailed him instantly. Fury detonated across his features. "You have the nerve to ask who I am?! I am—Jin Zixun!"

Recognition finally clicked. It was Jin Zixuan's cousin; he’d crossed paths with the loudmouth twice before.

Wei Wuxian’s heart sank like a stone. The lighthearted warmth that had filled his chest at the thought of celebrating his sister's newborn evaporated, replaced by a suffocating, ugly shadow. Still, he refused to let his mind plunge into the darkest conclusions—refusing to believe this ambush was what it looked like.

Jin Zixun bellowed from the cliff, "Wei Wuxian, I'm giving you one chance! Break the vile curse you put on me right now, and I might just let this slide without taking your head!"

Wei Wuxian blinked. Knowing full well it would sound like a deflection, he still had to ask: "What curse?"

Sure enough, Jin Zixun took it as brazen insolence. "Still playing dumb?!"

He aggressively ripped his embroidered collar open, roaring, "Look at this! See for yourself what kind of vile filth you planted on me!"

Across Jin Zixun’s chest was an endless, churning sea of dark, pitted craters!

The holes ranged from the size of tiny sesame seeds to bloated soybeans, peppered across his skin in a grotesque, festering lattice that made the gorge churn with nausea.

Wei Wuxian needed only a single glance. "The Curse of the Hundred Holes?"

"Damn right!" Jin Zixun spat. "The Hundred Holes!"

The Hundred Holes was an exceptionally insidious, vile blood curse.

Back during his youth in the Cloud Recesses, Wei Wuxian had idly flipped through an ancient forbidden tome detailing the technique. The illustration showed a man sitting with an eerily tranquil expression, completely numb to the rot, while coin-sized black holes festered across his flesh.

In the initial stages, the victim felt zero pain, usually brushing it off as coarse, irritated pores. But before long, the pinpricks swelled into sesame seeds, steadily widening and multiplying until the entire torso was riddled with dark cavities, turning the victim into a living, breathing sieve. Once the skin was saturated, the curse tunneled inward, corroding the internal organs—starting with blinding abdominal agony and ending in liquefied viscera!

To think Jin Zixun had been struck by a curse so nauseating and notoriously incurable actually pulled a fleeting flicker of pity from Wei Wuxian. Pity aside, however, the accusation was sheer lunacy. "You caught the Hundred Holes, so you ambush me? What does your rotting chest have to do with me?"

Repulsed by his own flesh, Jin Zixun yanked his robes shut. "Who else besides a crooked scoundrel who crawls through demonic gutters would wield something this venomous?!"

Literally dozens of people, Wei Wuxian thought dryly. Does this idiot honestly believe he’s well-liked?

Unwilling to stoke the flames and escalate the standoff, Wei Wuxian kept his tone level: "Jin Zixun, I don't dabble in petty gutter tricks. If I want someone dead, I make damn sure the entire world knows they died by my hand. And if I wanted you dead, your corpse would look a thousand times uglier than that."

Jin Zixun sneered, "Weren't you supposed to be an arrogant overlord? Now you're too cowardly to own your own work?"

"Why should I own something I didn't do?"

A murderous glint flared in Jin Zixun’s eyes. "I gave you the courtesy of a surrender. Since you refuse to turn back from the abyss, don't blame me for showing no mercy!"

Wei Wuxian’s eyes narrowed. "No mercy?"

The implication was crystal clear.

There were only two ways to break the Curse of the Hundred Holes: either the caster willingly severed their own cultivation to pull the curse back, or...

You slaughtered the caster outright!

Wei Wuxian let out a cold, derisive laugh. "No mercy? You? With this pathetic scrap of three hundred men?"

Jin Zixun raised his arm. Around the rim of the canyon, hundreds of bowstrings grooved taut, targeting the two figures pinned in the valley floor. Wei Wuxian raised Chenqing to his lips, a sharp, piercing melody cleaving the dead air.

Silence answered. Not a single corpse stirred.

Jin Zixun laughed mockingly, "We swept this entire gorge clean days ago just waiting for you to walk into the trap! You can blow that flute until your lungs burst—not a single soul is coming to your rescue! This canyon was paved specifically to be your grave!"

Wei Wuxian’s lips curved into a chilling smile. "You brought this on yourself."

The moment the words landed, Wen Ning’s hand shot up, snapping the red cord securing the suppression talisman around his throat!

With the ward shattered, his frame shuddered violently. His facial muscles twisted into a grotesque, jagged mask, dark, web-like fissures spider-webbing from his neck across his cheeks. Throwing his head back, an inhuman, deafening roar tore from his throat!

Many of the three hundred men stationed above were seasoned hunters, yet none had ever heard a fierce corpse unleash a sound so utterly apocalyptic; their knees nearly buckled on instinct. Even Jin Zixun’s scalp prickled with dread. Gritting his teeth, he swung his arm down: "Loose!"

Arrows rained down like a torrential storm!

Wen Ning pulverized a massive boulder with his bare hands, hoisting the stone slab overhead to swallow the incoming volley of iron. The second the barrage cleared, over a hundred swordsmen vaulted off the cliffs, blades drawn, swarming the valley floor. Wei Wuxian drifted back three paces, twisting his torso to dodge an opportunistic thrust from the side.

Jin Zixun had used the chaos to close the distance. Seeing Wei Wuxian without a sword, wielding only a flute that had been rendered useless in the sterilized canyon, he laughed wildly: "This is the price of your hubris! Facing steel without a blade—let's see you survive this!"

Wei Wuxian flicked his sleeve, sending a row of green-flamed talismans whistling through the air, their concussive bursts dimming the spiritual glare of Jin Zixun’s sword. The laughter caught in Jin Zixun’s throat as he scrambled to parry the spiritual fire.

As the two traded close-quarters blows, an object slipped from Wei Wuxian’s sleeve, tumbling into the air. Wei Wuxian froze, his gut clenching.

It was the gift for Jin Ling. Because he cherished it so deeply, terrified of crushing it in his pack and constantly wanting to pull it out to admire his handiwork, he had loosely tucked it into his inner cuff. The sudden grappling had jarred it loose, sending it sailing straight toward Jin Zixun.

Assuming it was a concealed poison or an explosive dart, Jin Zixun moved to dodge. But catching Wei Wuxian’s sudden, panicked expression, he changed his mind, snatching it out of the air. It was an exquisite little wooden box, carved with a line of delicate characters detailing Jin Ling’s name and birth coordinates. Jin Zixun blinked, then burst into uproarious, mocking laughter.

Wei Wuxian’s face went deadly pale, his voice scraping out like rusted iron: "Give it back."

Jin Zixun dangled the box between two fingers, dripping with scorn. "A gift for A-Ling?"

A few paces away, Wen Ning was tearing through the hundred cultivators like a demon possessed.

Jin Zixun sneered, "You didn't honestly believe you were going to attend A-Ling's banquet, did you?"

The sheer, venomous cruelty in that single question made Wei Wuxian’s hands tremble.

"Hold your hands!" a furious voice boomed from the cliffs above.

A white-robed silhouette glided down into the canyon, planting himself firmly between Wei Wuxian and Jin Zixun.

Jin Zixun gasped, "Zixuan?! What are you doing here?!"

Hand resting on the hilt of Suihua, Jin Zixuan’s eyes burned with incandescent rage. "What am I doing here?! What the hell are you doing?!"

"Where's A-Yao?" Jin Zixun demanded.

Jin Guangyao was supposed to be his backup. A year ago, Jin Zixun had treated the man like dirt beneath his boots, but with their relationship mended and the stakes raised, the address had smoothed into something familial.

Jin Zixuan snapped, "I had him locked down at Koi Tower! If I hadn't caught the panic on his face and forced the truth out of him, were you planning to orchestrate this slaughter behind my back?! You caught the Hundred Holes, and you didn't breathe a single word to me before staging a bloodbath?!"

Confessing the curse was a humiliating pill Jin Zixun couldn't swallow. He was handsome, vain, and strutted as a romantic gallant; the thought of anyone knowing his body was rotting with putrid holes made his skin crawl. More than that, catching a curse proved his spiritual defenses were paper-thin—a fatal flaw he couldn't let his peers see. Desperate, he had only confessionalized to Jin Guangshan, begging his uncle to secure the finest curse-breakers. But when the masters failed, and with Jin Ling's banquet approaching, Jin Zixuan had unexpectedly extended an invitation to Wei Wuxian. Jin Guangshan had hated the idea from the start, quietly advising Jin Zixun to turn the invitation into an ambush—cutting Wei Wuxian down on the road so he’d never taint Koi Tower.

Knowing Jin Zixuan was madly in love with Jiang Yanli and gossiped about every trivial affair with his wife, they had kept him completely in the dark, terrified he'd let the secret slip and scare Wei Wuxian away. Caught red-handed, Jin Zixun felt a fleeting pang of guilt, but his survival instincts roared louder: "Zixuan, keep this from your wife for now! Once I strip this rot from my chest, I'll kneel and beg her forgiveness!"

When Wei Wuxian had last laid eyes on Jin Zixuan, the young master had still carried the reckless arrogance of youth; now, married and grounded, his posture carried genuine weight. His jaw was set, his tone brokering no argument: "This situation can still be mediated. Stand down, both of you."

Jin Zixun flared up in hysterical frustration. "Mediated?! How can this be mediated?! Are you blind to what's happening to my body?!" He reached to tear his collar open again, but Jin Zixuan cut him off sharply: "Enough! Jin Guangyao already told me!"

"Then you should know I don't have time to waste!" Jin Zixun barked. "Are you honestly prioritizing your wife's brother over your own cousin's life?!"

"You know damn well that isn't who I am!" Jin Zixuan yelled back. "You haven't even proven the curse came from him—why this blind panic?! Wei Wuxian was formally invited by my hand to attend A-Ling's banquet! Acting like this—where do you leave my honor?! Where do you leave my wife's dignity?!"

Jin Zixun spat, "It's better he never sets foot in our home! What kind of filth is Wei Wuxian to sit at our family table?! Anyone who touches him gets dragged through the mud! Inviting him—aren't you terrified that you, your wife, and A-Ling will carry a permanent stain for the rest of your lives?!"

"Shut your mouth!" Jin Zixuan roared.

Spurred by pure venom, Jin Zixun tightened his fist.

Crack.

The small wooden box, along with the silver clarity bell and the jade tassel inside, was crushed to absolute powder!

Wei Wuxian watched the splintered dust spill from Jin Zixun's fingers, his pupils contracting to razor-thin needles. A concussive palm strike drove straight for Jin Zixun's skull! Oblivious to what the box contained, Jin Zixuan stepped in to parry the blow, shouting, "Wei Wuxian, haven't you had enough?!"

Wei Wuxian’s chest heaved violently, his eyes rimmed in burning scarlet. Jin Zixuan and Jin Zixun were blood cousins who had grown up together for two decades; Jin Zixuan couldn't simply turn his sword on his own kin for an outsider, especially when he held zero love for Wei Wuxian. Steadying his breath, Jin Zixuan reasoned, "Order Wen Ning to stop right now. Rein him in before this spirals out of control."

Wei Wuxian’s voice was a ragged, blood-soaked rasp: "...Why don't you tell them to stop first?"

All around them, cultivators were screaming, hacking, and dying.

Jin Zixuan yelled over the din, "Why must you stay this stubborn?! Calm down, come with me to Koi Tower, and face a proper inquiry! Lay the evidence bare—if you didn't do it, no one will touch you!"

Wei Wuxian let out a bitter, venomous laugh. "Stand down? The second I tell Wen Ning to stand down, three hundred arrows will punch through my chest and tear me to pieces! And you want me to walk up to Koi Tower for an 'inquiry'?!"

"I won't let that happen!"

"You won't let it happen?!" Wei Wuxian mocked. "What guarantee do you have?! Jin Zixuan, answer me this: when you invited me, did you truly have no idea they planned to butcher me on the road?!"

Jin Zixuan stared in stunned outrage. "You—Wei Wuxian, are you completely insane?!"

Swallowing down an inferno of hatred, Wei Wuxian whispered, "Get out of my way, Jin Zixuan. I won't touch you, but don't you dare push me."

Seeing him refuse to yield an inch, Jin Zixuan lunged forward, hands outstretched to physically restrain him: "Why can't you just swallow your pride for once?! A-Li is—"

The moment his fingers reached for Wei Wuxian's robes, a sickening, wet crunch tore through the air.

It was impossibly close. Jin Zixuan froze.

Slowly lowering his gaze, he stared down at the pale, blood-drenched arm punching clean through his own sternum.

Without anyone noticing, Wen Ning had ghosted behind him, a few splatters of scorching, crimson gore painting the dead gray of his cheek.

Jin Zixuan’s lips parted faintly, his eyes wide and vacant. Yet, clinging to his dying breath, he forced out the remainder of the sentence he had started:

"...She's... still waiting for you... to come to Koi Tower... for A-Ling's banquet..."

Wei Wuxian stood completely paralyzed, his expression matching the hollow shock on the dying man's face.

His mind refused to process the scene.

What just happened?

How did everything shatter in a single heartbeat?

No.

This wasn't right.

Something went wrong.

Wen Ning pulled his hand back, leaving a gaping, hollow crater through Jin Zixuan’s chest.

Jin Zixuan’s face gave an agonizing, pathetic twitch, as though he believed the wound was minor, as though he could still stand on his own two feet. But his knees buckled, collapsing heavily into the dirt.

A chorus of shrill, hysterical shrieks tore through the canyon:

"The... the Ghost General has gone berserk!"

"He killed him! Wei Wuxian ordered the Ghost General to murder Jin Zixuan!"

Jin Zixun screamed like a dying animal, "Fire! What are you standing there for?! FIRE THE ARROWS!"

As he turned to run, a black blur closed the distance like a phantom. A pale, freezing hand clamped around his throat with crushing force.

"Aaaaaaaagh—!!!"

Wei Wuxian stood frozen amidst the carnage, completely unmoving.

No.

That wasn't it.

He had been controlling Wen Ning. He was keeping him on a leash!

Even in a berserk state, he should have been able to pull him back!

He had always controlled him perfectly. Always!

He never wanted Jin Zixuan dead.

He held zero intention of killing him! But in that split second, for reasons he couldn't comprehend, his grip had slipped... the control had simply snapped!

Jin Zixuan’s body gave out entirely, pitching forward with a dull, heavy thud against the stones.

A man who had spent his entire life cloaked in aristocratic pride, obsessed with his appearance, pristine to the point of fastidious cleanliness, was now splayed face-down in the blood-soaked dirt. The red gore splattered across his cheek matched the exact crimson shade of the vermilion mark centered on his brow.

Staring into those dimming, lifeless pupils, Wei Wuxian’s skull threatened to split open. The canyon around him had dissolved into a shrieking, blood-drenched abattoir, but his ears caught none of it.

The only sound echoing through his soul was a feral, screaming voice tearing him apart:

Didn't you claim you had everything under control?!

Didn't you swear you could rein it in?!

Didn't you promise that nothing would ever go wrong, that you would never fail?!!!

His mind went black. When his eyelids finally tore open, his vision was greeted by the familiar, damp stone ceiling of the Demon-Subduing Cave.

Wen Qing and Wen Ning were both inside.

Wen Ning’s pupils had settled back into the centers of his eyes, having slipped out of his berserk state. He was murmuring something in a hushed whisper to his sister, but the moment he saw Wei Wuxian stir, he dropped silently to his knees. Wen Qing stood beside him, her eyes rimmed in raw crimson, entirely silent.

Wei Wuxian sat up.

After a suffocating pause, a tidal wave of unadulterated hatred detonated in his chest.

He planted a brutal kick straight into Wen Ning’s chest, sending the fierce corpse crashing across the stone floor.

Wen Qing flinched, her fists clenching white-knuckled, but she kept her head bowed, biting her lip.

Wei Wuxian roared, "Who did you kill?! Do you have any idea who you killed?!"

Right at that moment, little Wen Yuan came waddling into the cavern, the woven grass butterfly proudly balanced on his head, beaming from ear to ear. "Xian-gege..."

He had run in eager to show off the new colors he’d painted onto his toy, but stepping across the threshold, he ran smack into a terrifying, demonic Wei Wuxian and a cowering Wen Ning. The toddler froze, paralyzed.

Wei Wuxian whipped his head around, his furious gaze wild and unchecked. Terrified out of his wits, Wen Yuan jumped, the butterfly sliding off his head and tumbling to the dirt as he burst into hysterical, screaming tears. Fourth Uncle rushed in with a stooped back, scooping the boy up and frantically carrying him out.

Wen Ning dragged himself back onto his knees, head bowed, terrified to breathe. Wei Wuxian lunged forward, grabbing him by the collar and hoisting him into the air, screaming into his face: "You could have killed anyone else! Anyone! Why did it have to be Jin Zixuan?!"

Watching from the side, Wen Qing desperately wanted to shield her brother, but she forced herself to stay back, weeping in silent, helpless terror.

Wei Wuxian shook him violently. "You killed him—what is my Shijie supposed to do?! What is her son supposed to do?! What am I supposed to do?! What the hell am I supposed to do?!"

His roars echoed off the cavern walls like rolling thunder, carrying outside until Wen Yuan’s distant crying grew even more frantic.

Listening to the toddler's muffled wails, staring at the terrified siblings who didn't even know where to put their hands, Wei Wuxian’s heart sank into pitch-black despair.

He interrogated his own soul: Why on earth did I trap myself on this godforsaken Burial Mounds all these years? Why did I have to swallow all this misery? Why did I insist on walking this path in the first place? Why did I reduce myself to this wretched state? How does the world see me now? What did I actually gain from any of this?! Am I insane?! Have I completely lost my mind?!

If only I had never stepped onto this road in the first place.

A soft, trembling voice broke the silence. "...I'm... sorry."

It was a dead man. He possessed no facial expressions, his eyes couldn't flush with tears, and his tear ducts couldn't produce moisture. Yet right now, the agony etched across that corpse's face was unmistakably, heartbreakingly real.

Wen Ning choked out the words, over and over:

"I'm sorry...

"It's... it's all my fault...

"I'm sorry..."

Listening to the stammered, endless apologies, an overwhelming wave of absurd, bitter hilarity washed over Wei Wuxian.

It wasn't Wen Ning's fault.

It was his own damn fault.

In a berserk state, Wen Ning was nothing more than a weapon. And the creator of that weapon was Wei Wuxian. The commands he followed were Wei Wuxian's own subconscious malice.

The killing intent had choked the canyon, and Wei Wuxian had never bothered hiding his deep-seated hatred for Jin Zixuan in front of Wen Ning. The second Jin Zixuan raised a hand to grab him, Wen Ning's mindless instincts had flagged the man as an "enemy"—executing the directive to slaughter without a second thought.

He was the one who had failed to control his own weapon. He was the one blinded by his own arrogant hubris. He was the one who had ignored every single warning sign up until this day, foolishly believing he could suppress any flare of chaos.

Wen Ning was a weapon, but had he ever asked to be forged into one?

Could a man so timid, gentle, and terrified of conflict truly find joy in butchering people under Wei Wuxian’s command?

Back then, when Jiang Yanli had gifted him a single bowl of lotus root soup, Wen Ning had carried it all the way up the mountain without spilling a drop. He couldn't drink it himself, yet he had watched the others finish it with pure delight, excitedly asking what it tasted like so he could imagine the flavor. Having murdered Jiang Yanli's husband with his own hands—did anyone honestly think he was suffering any less?

Taking all the blame onto his own shoulders, and turning around to beg for forgiveness.

Clutching Wen Ning’s collar, staring into that pale, lifeless face, the image of Jin Zixuan suddenly flashed before Wei Wuxian’s eyes—covered in grime and gore, just as pale, and just as utterly lifeless.

He remembered Jiang Yanli, who had finally found happiness with the man she loved. He remembered her newborn son, A-Ling—the child he had personally named, who had just clutched his father's sword at his one-year ceremony, sending his parents over the moon. In two days, it was supposed to be his full-month banquet.

Lost in the spiraling nightmare, tears suddenly spilled down Wei Wuxian’s cheeks.

He stared into the void, murmuring in broken, ragged despair: "...Can someone please tell me... what the hell am I supposed to do now?"
